newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end down, discouraged by scandal worry.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end down, discouraged by scandal worry.

text.p: Tokyo stocks ended Wednesday trade lower, discouraged by worries that more big brokerages could be involved in a payoff scandal ensnaring Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
Worries grew after Tokyo prosecutors' raided Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd in the morning, brokers said.
The 225-share Nikkei average finished 189.92 points or 0.93 percent lower at 20,212.82. Its September futures closed down 180 points at 20,220.

"There were glimmers of hope that with the announcement of punitive measures against Nomura and Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd today, the market would be able to breathe a small sigh of relief," said Akihiro Naemura, Okasan Securities general manager.
The Yamaichi raid and reports of the possible involvement of others raised worries but as the market was expecting something of the sort the impact was limited, he added.

Yamaichi was the most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse with volume of 6.32 million shares. It renewed its calendar 1997 low, sagging to 275 yen in the morning, but ended at 280 yen, down 21.

A government source told reporters that Yamaichi had "generally" admitted to illegally paying compensation for losses incurred by a corporate client linked to the racketeer at the core of the scandal.
Among other "Big Four" brokers, Daiwa Securities lost 40 yen to end at 825 and Nikko Securities fell 21 to 670.
Nomura was flat at 1,580.
Compared to Nomura, market sources said Yamaichi, which is financially weaker, may find it harder to absorb the penalties which could be imposed.

"I think the result (of the scandal) ultimately is a positive one if they (Yamaichi) move to more transparency, but it could be a rough ride getting there," said James McGinnis, financial analyst at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson International.
Market sources however said they were more concerned about the possibility of more brokerages becoming entangled in the scandal. Shares of DKB lost 20 to end at 1,480.

"If dealing for their own accounts, for example, were to be suspended for all four brokerages, turnover would diminish even more and hurt investor sentiment in general," said Shinichi Ichikawa, a strategist at Credit Lyonnais Securities.
However, some speculated that it would take time before other brokerages were raided.

"In order to make the listing of Central Japan Railway in October a success, the Finance Ministry is going to be very cautious about investigations and raids against other brokerages as such events hurt investor sentiment and could depress the market," a trader at a foreign brokerage said.
Turnover was 364 million shares, compared to 343 million shares on Tuesday. Losers swamped losers 851 to 236, while 138 shares were unchanged.

Japanese industrial production data, which was released in the afternoon, was weak, but still came in within expectations and did not affect the market greatly. brokers said, adding that the market was hoping fervently for signs of a pick-up in the economy in the coming months.
Despite the indices' losses, a small number of blue chip shares fared well, with TDK Corp jumping to a record high of 10,100 yen before ending at 9,950 yen, up 250.
"It's the same bellwether issues being bought day after day by the same large-lot investors," one trader said. "It is preventing the market from plunging on bad news but this can't go on forever."

Profit-taking helped widen losses in the afternoon as well as did selling of low-priced, large capital issues, brokers said. Sony Corp renewed its record high, reaching 11,900 yen before slipping 100 yen on profit-taking to 11,600.
Brokers said for the time being, the Nikkei average was likely to hover near the 20,500 level, as investors continue to buy firms that are little influenced by domestic woes.

By sector, transport equipment, real estate, oil, rubber and securities were the top losers. Electric equipment, miscellaneous manufacturers, insurance, gas and automobiles headed the list of gainers.

The TOPIX index fell 11.96 points or 0.77 percent to 1,536.92. The Nikkei 300 shed 2.56 points or 0.85 percent to 300.04. The second section index fell 7.04 points or 0.40 percent to 1,770.33. Second section turnover was 7.53 million shares against 7.28 million on the previous day.
The over-the-counter index fell 7.51 points or 0.66 percent to 1,129.85.--Masako Iijima, Tokyo Equities Desk
